name: Azuchi Screens
subcategory: Japanese artwork gifted to the Vatican

description:
The  Azuchi Screens  (Japanese: 安土図屏風) are a pair of six-panel folding-screens, one depicting Azuchi Castle and the other its nearby town. Oda Nobunaga gifted them to Alessandro Valignano and, via the Tenshō Embassy, they were presented to Pope Gregory XIII. They were displayed in the Vatican collections, where they were admired by visitors. However, they disappeared from historical record. Their fate is unknown and they are considered to be lost. The screens were seminal works in the development of Japanese folding screens.

Variations on the name are Azuchiyama screens (安土山図屏風) or Azuchi Castle screens (安土城図屏風).
